reference.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students / Scott-Brown's Otorhinolaryngology
clinicalPearls: Inferior concha is an independent facial bone; middle and superior conchae are ethmoid bone projections
Frontal, maxillary and anterior ethmoidal sinuses drain into the middle meatus via the ostiomeatal complex
Nasolacrimal duct drains exclusively into the inferior meatus under the valve of Hasner
Kiesselbach plexus (Little area) on the anterior nasal septum is the site of 90% of epistaxis episodes
Cribriform plate fractures cause CSF rhinorrhea (high beta-2 transferrin) and anosmia with risk of bacterial meningitis
reference.pathophysiology: The nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses condition, filter and humidify inspired air while reducing skull weight and providing vocal resonance. The ostiomeatal complex is a critical drainage bottleneck. Mucosal edema from viral rhinitis or allergic inflammation obstructs the maxillary sinus ostium, precipitating secondary acute bacterial rhinosinusitis with Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae.
additionalInvestigations: Non-contrast coronal CT of paranasal sinuses for ostiomeatal patency
Nasal endoscopy with 0-degree and 30-degree rigid endoscopes
Beta-2 transferrin assay on clear nasal fluid to confirm CSF leak
